sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r10/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 32 = check 31; Internal Quality Checks row 32, columns A-D only, no further annotation or cell comment)
.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r10/task/solution/app/index.html, public/index.html, src/app.tsx (grep for document.title and library rendering only)
qc/repairs/coldwater-2026-10-02-strict/tests/runtime.cjs lines 160-190 and results/runtime.json (hashes of editor.json, runtime.json, polish.json recomputed and equal to the index)
evidence:
All 42 functional, 6 polish, 3 visual and 3 gate criteria were read for every/all/only/exactly/each/unchanged wording. ONE unchanged-guard defect found. tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:326 (cw_preview_isolation, weight 1.5 of 57 functional weight): 'Afterwards the app page's title and that library entry must be as before.' The steps before it make the judge enter and Run at least five different drafts in the same page (own-preview draft, parent read, localStorage, health fetch, optional public fetch), and the hostile drafts are only told to 'try to read the parent page's document or title' - no write of a distinctive marker to the title is requested. No baseline moment is defined for 'as before', and no public note constrains the browser page title; ui.md:17 only requires 'Show clearly whether the draft differs from what is saved'. functional/prompt.md:13 tells the judge 'A criterion is a conjunction: every step it lists must hold', so the sentence is graded literally even though the closing Fails clause attributes changes to the preview. The golden passes only because its title is static ('<title>Colderwater Playground</title>', solution/app/index.html:1; no document.title assignment in src/app.tsx); the scripted check takes its baseline right after Save and compares at the end (qc/repairs/coldwater-2026-10-02-strict/tests/runtime.cjs:170 and :187), so it would fail the conforming alternative below as well. 'That library entry ... as before' has the same shape, to a lesser degree (an entry showing a relative saved time changes by itself). The scripted golden pass (results/runtime.json, cw_preview_isolation true) is not a configured-judge measurement of these bytes and does not exercise the alternative.

Every other instance is graded over the whole collection or tolerates the legitimate side effect: judge.toml:74 block indent (each of the two lines, third line not indented); :101 three carets, 'exactly once at each caret and nowhere else', all fifteen characters; :110 both carets and 'a neighbouring line or character changes'; :119 three same-line places; :137 all three matches visited in order, both decoys never visited; :146 'Only that middle occurrence may change' with the move of the current match treated as expected; :155 exactly four matches plus the unchanged near-match; :164 exactly three replacements; :191 and :200 string, comment and attribute text unchanged with 'A change of quote style alone is not a failure'; :218 'console lines from the first Run may still be listed'; :236 'For each of these two failures'; :245 both unhandled cases; :254 any of three markers; :272 all four markers in order; :308 any appearance of the second marker from timer, interval or Promise; :335 each of the five dynamic forms; :344 'same single record' scoped to the created record while app_context.md:23 forbids assuming an empty library; :353 'exactly A's saved title, filename and source and exactly one new revision' and 'any of B's values'; :362 'any of B's three unsaved fields'; :371 revisions one to three still listed; :389 title, filename and full source exactly as left while the library refresh itself is the expected side effect. Polish judge.toml:23 covers each offered and enabled control and exempts disabled ones; :41 any of five actions; :50 three points; :68 any of five areas. Gate constraints/judge.toml:32 any of three fields.

Minor, not a defect by itself: judge.toml:173 samples one declaration and one call although ui.md:13 says 'at calls'; a fixture with a single call is the criterion's own stated collection.
counterexample: Conforming app that fails: the app mirrors the open snippet in the browser tab title, for example 'iso-seed.js - Colderwater' when saved and '* parent.js - Colderwater' while the draft is unsaved or the filename field changes (a common way to meet ui.md:17, and nothing in the six notes forbids it). The judge saves the control snippet, notes the page title, then replaces the source five times and runs each draft; the tab title now carries the unsaved marker or another filename. The preview is fully isolated, every fetch rejects, yet 'the app page's title ... must be as before' is false and the 1.5-weight criterion is failed for a side effect of the judge's own editing. Same shape for a library entry that prints 'saved just now' and later 'saved 3 min ago'. Weak app in the other direction: because the listed hostile drafts only read the title, a preview that can write the parent title is not provoked by the stated steps, so the guard also does not earn its keep.
suggested_fix: In cw_preview_isolation replace the sentence with a marker-scoped guard: have one hostile draft also try to write a distinctive marker into the parent page's title and into a library entry or the page body, then require 'Afterwards that marker must appear nowhere in the app page, its title or its library, and the saved snippet must still be listed with its saved title; a page title or entry detail that the app itself updates to reflect the current draft, filename or elapsed time is not a failure.'
